title: Event Playbook
description: A data-driven event planning guide that turns answers into dated, assignable tasks, operational advisories and reusable event knowledge.

deadlineCodes.label: Initial planning
deadlineCodes.description: Initial planning milestone, normally around 60 days before the event.

deadlineCodes.label: Detailed planning
deadlineCodes.description: Detailed planning milestone, normally around 20 days before the event.

deadlineCodes.label: Final arrangements
deadlineCodes.description: Final arrangements milestone, normally around one week before the event.

deadlineCodes.label: Commitment decision
deadlineCodes.description: The go-ahead required before additional staffing, purchasing, suppliers or outward communications are firmly committed.

deadlineCodes.label: Final checks
deadlineCodes.description: Final checks milestone, normally the day before the event.

deadlineCodes.label: Final go/no-go
deadlineCodes.description: The final operational confirmation that the event is proceeding, with one decision owner and one communications route.

deadlineCodes.label: Change response
deadlineCodes.description: Immediate coordinated action when an event is cancelled or postponed.

deadlineCodes.label: Immediate follow-up
deadlineCodes.description: Immediate close-down and follow-up work, normally the day after the event.

deadlineCodes.label: Post-event review
deadlineCodes.description: Post-event review and retrospective, normally one week after the event.

modules.title: Start here
modules.description: Define the event and decide which specialist planning modules are required.

items.label: What is the provisional event date?
Does it involve golf?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether the event involves golf
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the event organiser and Golf team, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Will any clubhouse room or area need to be reserved, prepared or rearranged for the event?
items.helpText: Choose Yes for room reservations, seating changes, a top table, room dressing or operational television and audio-visual setup.

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether a clubhouse room or area needs to be reserved, prepared or rearranged
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the event organiser and Clubhouse team, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Does entertainment need to be organised for this event?
items.helpText: This includes a club playlist, a DJ, live performers, a guest speaker, a host or any other programmed social activity.

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether entertainment needs to be organised
dontKnowTask.detail: Agree the intended atmosphere and programme with the organiser, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Will food or drink need to be planned specifically for the event?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide if food or drink needs to be planned specifically for the event
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the event organiser and Food & Beverage team, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Will attendees need to book to come to the event and/or will they be charged?
items.helpText: Choose Yes if attendees must book, register, reserve or confirm a place, if they will pay an entry charge, or both. This opens the Bookings and Tickets planning area. It does not cover optional bar or food purchases or routine golf fees.

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether attendees need to book and/or pay for entry
dontKnowTask.detail: Confirm whether attendance must be reserved or registered and whether an entry charge is needed, then return to this question before booking arrangements or publicity begin.

items.label: Will the event need to be advertised or communicated to members, visitors or attendees?
items.helpText: Choose Yes to decide whether to use the clubhouse screens, member email, social media or the Member Diary, and to create the corresponding Communications Centre work.

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether the event needs advertising or attendee communications
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the event organiser and Communications team, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Will there be prizes, presentations, speeches or a formal welcome?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether prizes, presentations, speeches or a formal welcome will be included
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the event organiser and relevant club teams, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Will this event require event-specific staffing, volunteer cover, rota changes or named operational duties?
items.helpText: Choose Yes for additional people, changed or extended shifts, or named responsibility for opening, setup, service, handovers, close-down or lock-up.
items.example: An extra bar shift, volunteers staffing registration, an early-opening keyholder or somebody remaining to lock up.

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether the event needs staffing changes, volunteer cover or named operational duties
dontKnowTask.detail: Check the full event timetable with the organiser and affected department leads, including setup and lock-up, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Does the event need a specific safety, safeguarding or contingency review?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether the event needs a specific safety, safeguarding or contingency review
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the event organiser and responsible club leads, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

modules.title: Event viability and change control
modules.description: Set the decision authority, agree when commitments can be made and coordinate any cancellation or postponement through one source of truth.

items.label: Who has authority to make the final go/no-go decision?
items.helpText: Name one person. Department leads should not have to infer whether the event is proceeding from separate conversations.

items.label: Who owns the single authoritative message if the event changes?
items.helpText: This person coordinates the wording and audience so operational and member messages do not conflict.

items.label: What could cause the event to be cancelled, postponed or placed at risk?
If attendance is a viability trigger, what minimum attendance would make the event viable?
items.helpText: Optional. Leave this blank if there is no fixed number and the decision will be made case by case.

items.label: Which teams or commitments must be checked before the event status changes?

options.label: Ticket sales, admission payments or refunds

items.label: Will extra staffing, purchasing or supplier commitments be made specifically for this event?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether the event requires extra staffing, purchasing or supplier commitments
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the affected department leads and record what will become difficult or costly to reverse.

items.label: Have members or participants already been told that this event is proceeding?

dontKnowTask.title: Check whether any event communications have already been sent or scheduled
dontKnowTask.detail: Check member email, organiser messages, clubhouse screens, booking confirmations and social channels.

items.title: Review and confirm the event's go/no-go plan
items.detail: Check the recorded decision owner, communications owner, viability triggers, optional attendance threshold and affected teams. Correct anything that is missing or wrong, then confirm the plan.

reviewSummary.title: Current go/no-go plan
reviewSummary.instruction: The Event Coordinator reviews these answers. Reassign this task only if someone else will perform the check.

fields.label: Final decision owner
fields.emptyText: Choose the person who can make the final decision

fields.label: Change communications owner
fields.emptyText: Choose who will issue the authoritative update

fields.label: Go/no-go triggers
fields.emptyText: Record what could stop or place the event at risk

fields.label: Minimum viable attendance
fields.emptyText: No fixed threshold - decide case by case
fields.notApplicableText: Not applicable - attendance is not a go/no-go trigger

fields.label: Teams and commitments to check
fields.emptyText: Select the affected teams or commitments

fields.label: Extra commitments planned
fields.emptyText: Confirm whether extra commitments will be made

fields.label: Members already told it is proceeding
fields.emptyText: Confirm whether communications have already been sent

items.title: Confirm the event is proceeding before additional staffing, purchasing, suppliers or publicity are firmly committed
items.detail: The decision owner should mark the event Confirmed or At risk and tell affected department leads before irreversible commitments are made.

items.title: Give Food & Beverage an explicit event go-ahead before arranging extra cover, ordering stock or messaging members
items.detail: F&B should work from the current Playbook status rather than a separate organiser conversation.

items.title: Confirm the event status and agreed wording before sending or scheduling member promotion
items.detail: All departments and the organiser should use the same approved event status and communications owner.

items.title: Record the final go/no-go decision and confirm it with every operational lead
items.detail: Do not rely on silence as confirmation. Mark the event Confirmed, At risk, Postponed or Cancelled in the Playbook.

items.title: Resolve the at-risk event decision and issue one status update
items.detail: Review the recorded risk with the decision owner and either confirm, postpone or cancel the event.

items.title: Coordinate the cancellation or postponement and confirm every interested party has been told
items.detail: The event organiser owns this action. Use the recorded status, reason and agreed wording as the single source of truth, then confirm receipt with everyone already briefed or committed.

items.title: Review and, where possible, cancel additional Food & Beverage cover, extended hours and event-specific preparation
items.detail: This task appears because the plan records F&B work or a briefing. Confirm what was actually arranged, what can be cancelled, reused or returned, and any unavoidable cost.

items.title: Review and release or revise clubhouse rooms, service arrangements and event setup
items.detail: This task appears because completed work, notes or a sent briefing indicate that clubhouse arrangements may already exist.

items.title: Review and release or revise tee times, competition arrangements and course preparation
items.detail: This task appears because a tee-time reservation, completed work, notes or a sent briefing indicates that golf or course arrangements may already exist.

items.title: Stop or replace scheduled event publicity, clubhouse screen artwork and outstanding messages
items.detail: Check the member email schedule, clubhouse screens, booking confirmations and any organiser-managed channels.

items.title: Cancel, postpone or rebook the entertainer or speaker and confirm the financial impact
items.detail: Use the recorded supplier terms, notify the provider through one named contact, release any hired equipment or access arrangements, and record deposits, cancellation fees or replacement-date commitments in Event Finances.

items.title: Close booking, registration and ticket-sales routes for the changed event
items.detail: Close or amend every booking or sales route, preserve the attendee and purchaser records, and make sure public links show the same cancellation or postponement status.

items.title: Identify everyone who paid and complete the agreed refunds or ticket transfers
items.detail: Reconcile all payment routes against the purchaser list, apply the published policy consistently, tell purchasers what will happen and record refunds, retained fees or transferred income in Event Finances.

items.title: Issue one authoritative cancellation or postponement update to members and participants
items.detail: Use the wording recorded with the event status. It should replace, not compete with, earlier operational or organiser messages.

items.title: Agree a replacement date or close the postponed event
items.detail: When a new date is known, update the event date and milestones, then return the status to Provisional or Confirmed.

items.title: Record the operational, financial and communication impact of the late change
items.detail: Capture avoidable cost, member confusion and any process change for the next event.

modules.title: Golf
modules.description: Tee-time planning, competition setup, course preparation, registration and golf-day operations.

items.label: Are the required tee times already reserved?
items.helpText: The event date is already fixed. This confirms whether the course allocation for that date has actually been secured.

items.label: Who should arrange the tee-time reservation?

items.title: Agree and reserve the required tee-time allocation with H&C
items.detail: If H&C cannot accommodate the required allocation, return to the event details and reconsider the event date before the rest of the plan is progressed.

items.title: Ask the Professional Shop to reserve the required tee times
items.detail: Confirm the first and last tee-time allocation and any restrictions that apply.

items.title: Arrange the required tee-time allocation for the event
items.detail: The event or section organiser is responsible for securing the tee-time allocation and confirming it in the plan.

items.label: What type of golf is involved?
How many holes will competitors play?
How many holes will actually be played?
items.helpText: Use this for unusual events such as the seven-hole Steeple Chase.

items.label: How many players are taking part?
items.helpText: Include every competitor expected to return to the clubhouse after play.

items.label: How many parents, guardians or other supporters should we plan for around the finish?
items.helpText: Enter 0 if no supporters are expected. This is combined with the player count to estimate clubhouse demand.

items.label: How long do you expect one group to take to complete the round?
items.helpText: Use the likely pace for this age group, competition format and number of holes. This duration drives the expected clubhouse return time.

items.label: How will players start?
What is the first and last tee time?
items.helpText: These times are used to estimate when the first and last groups will return to the clubhouse.

items.label: What time is the shotgun start?
items.helpText: A shotgun start creates a much more concentrated return to the clubhouse because most players finish at around the same time.

items.title: Expected clubhouse return
items.body: The Playbook combines the expected round duration, start pattern, player count and supporter count to forecast the return time and likely operational impact.

items.label: What competition format will be used?
Describe the competition format

items.title: Confirm the competition format, tees, handicap rules and scoring arrangements

items.label: Will results need to be calculated, published or announced on the day?

items.title: Assign responsibility for collecting scores, calculating results and producing the final result

staffBriefing.instruction: Collect scores, calculate the results and have the final result ready for the presentation.

items.label: Are any additional golf fees or payments due on the day?
items.helpText: For example golf-competition entry fees, sweep payments or visitor green fees. This is separate from any charge for admission to the event.

items.label: What needs to be paid, collected or reconciled?

items.title: Confirm how event-day golf fees will be collected and reconciled

staffBriefing.instruction: Collect the agreed event-day golf fees and retain the information needed for reconciliation.

items.label: Does the course need any non-standard setup, signage, markers, equipment or hole arrangements?
What non-standard course requirements are involved?

options.label: Special hole setup / obstacles / unusual features
Special tees, markers or course markings
Equipment or consumables to purchase (for example glow sticks)

items.label: Describe the non-standard course setup
items.helpText: Record enough detail that the course team and event organiser know exactly what has to be installed, moved, purchased, printed or removed.

items.title: Agree and document the complete non-standard course setup
Prepare and position all required on-course signage

staffBriefing.instruction: Position all agreed on-course signage before players arrive.

items.title: Prepare and position the selected competition markers
items.detail: Confirm the relevant holes and position the nearest-to-the-pin and/or longest-drive markers before play.

staffBriefing.instruction: Position the agreed nearest-the-pin and longest-drive markers on the correct holes.

items.title: Print, prepare or obtain the event-specific scorecards or route cards
items.detail: Confirm whether the cards need to be produced internally or obtained from an external competition provider such as the Golf Foundation, then have the correct quantity ready before play.

items.title: Purchase or source all non-standard course equipment and consumables
items.detail: Examples include glow sticks, temporary markers, novelty obstacles, lighting equipment or event-specific materials.

items.title: Brief the Greens Team and schedule installation of special hole features

items.label: Where will players check in or sign in on arrival?

items.title: Prepare and staff the player registration / sign-in point

staffBriefing.instruction: Set up the player registration or sign-in point and have it staffed before arrivals begin.

items.label: Is arrival signage needed outside or inside the clubhouse to direct players to registration?

items.title: Prepare and position arrival and registration signage

staffBriefing.instruction: Position the agreed arrival and registration signage before guests arrive.

items.label: Is a starter or first-tee marshal required?

items.title: Assign a starter or first-tee marshal and provide the event briefing

staffBriefing.instruction: Manage the first tee and start players in accordance with the agreed event format and timings.

items.label: Are on-course marshals required?
items.helpText: Consider pace of play, unusual routes, safety pinch points, junior supervision and special-format events.

items.title: Recruit, position and brief the required on-course marshals

staffBriefing.instruction: Cover the agreed on-course positions and follow the event lead's safety and escalation instructions.

modules.title: Presentation and prizes
modules.description: Trophies, prizes, presentation equipment, prize-table setup and the formal running order.

items.label: Are prizes, trophies, vouchers or awards required?
What needs to be presented?
What prizes are required, including the winner categories, quantities and values?
items.helpText: Record enough detail to obtain the correct prizes and approve the overall cost, for example winner, runner-up, nearest the pin, quantity and value.

items.title: Agree the exact prize categories, quantities, values and overall budget
items.detail: Confirm the prize specification with the organiser before anything is ordered, purchased or allocated from existing stock.

items.label: Does a trophy need to be retrieved from the trophy cabinet?

items.title: Retrieve the correct trophy, check its condition and have it ready for presentation

items.label: If it is not in the trophy cabinet, how will the trophy or cup be obtained?

options.label: Collect an existing trophy held elsewhere
Order a new trophy through the Professional Shop
Purchase a new trophy externally through Finance / Accounts

items.title: Collect the existing trophy from its current holder and check its condition
items.detail: Confirm who holds it, when it will be returned and whether cleaning, repair or engraving is required before presentation.

items.label: Who will provide the physical prizes, merchandise, medals or awards?
items.helpText: The Professional Shop is normally the first option, but prizes can instead be bought externally or allocated from items already held.

options.label: Already held by the club or organiser

items.title: Confirm the prizes already held are suitable, complete and reserved for the event
items.detail: Check quantities, condition and location so replacements can still be obtained if anything is missing.

items.title: Order the agreed prizes, trophies, medals or vouchers through the Professional Shop
items.detail: Give the Professional Shop the approved specification and confirm availability, cost, delivery or collection date and how the club will be charged.

items.title: Approve and arrange payment for prizes or vouchers ordered through the Professional Shop
items.detail: Confirm the approved amount, payment method and the invoice or internal charge needed for reconciliation.

items.title: Purchase the agreed external prizes, trophies or vouchers
items.detail: Confirm the supplier, face value or specification, total cost, delivery date and evidence required for payment reconciliation.

items.title: Authorise, prepare and account for the cash or monetary prizes
items.detail: Confirm each amount, how it will be issued, who will hold it before presentation and how receipt or collection will be recorded.

items.title: Agree how the other prizes or awards will be sourced and paid for
items.detail: Record the owner, supplier or holder, approved cost and the date by which each item must be available.

items.label: Do prizes or trophies need winner labels, place cards or presentation notes?

items.title: Prepare winner labels, place cards and presentation notes for the prizes

items.label: Does a prize / trophy table need to be set up?

items.title: Arrange the approved prizes and presentation display on the prepared table
items.detail: Once the Clubhouse team has prepared the table and agreed covering, lay out the trophies, prizes and winner labels before the presentation starts.

staffBriefing.instruction: Once the table and covering are ready, lay out the trophies, prizes and winner labels before the presentation.

items.label: Will a microphone or PA system be needed for the presentation or announcements?

items.title: Set up and test the microphone / PA system before the presentation

staffBriefing.instruction: Set up and test the microphone or PA system before it is needed.

items.label: Does someone need to host the presentation, welcome guests or announce prizes?
items.helpText: This is about presentation duties. A guest or after-dinner speaker is planned separately in Entertainment.

items.title: Assign the presentation host and prepare the running order, winners and key announcements

staffBriefing.instruction: Follow the agreed presentation running order and make the welcome, winner and prize announcements.

items.label: Should photographs be taken of winners, trophies or the presentation?

items.title: Assign someone to take the required presentation photographs and confirm the shots needed

staffBriefing.instruction: Take the agreed photographs of winners, trophies and the presentation.

modules.title: Entertainment and event production
modules.description: Shape the social programme, decide who will deliver it, arrange performers or speakers, and coordinate payment, room and technical requirements.

items.label: What entertainment or programmed social activity is being considered?

options.label: Background music or a club playlist

items.label: What experience are we trying to create, and what should actually happen?
items.helpText: Describe the audience, atmosphere, programme, approximate timings and any important content or restrictions.

items.label: Who will provide the entertainment?

options.label: An external entertainer, speaker or supplier
A mixture of internal and external people

items.title: Agree the entertainment brief, audience, running times and working budget
items.detail: Turn the initial idea into a clear programme that can be quoted, booked, staffed, promoted and delivered.

items.title: Decide whether the entertainment will be delivered internally or by an external provider
items.detail: Compare the available people, quality, cost, equipment and operational risk before committing to the delivery route.

items.label: How will the music be provided?

options.label: A club-managed playlist using house equipment
A live singer, musician or band
Music supplied by another entertainer or organiser

items.title: Prepare, approve and test the event playlist on the clubhouse sound system
items.detail: Confirm who controls the music, the required content and timings, volume limits, playback device, internet dependency and a backup option.

staffBriefing.instruction: Run the approved event playlist at the agreed times and volume, with the backup source available.

items.label: How will the guest speaker be arranged?

options.label: A club member, officer or staff speaker
An invited external speaker with no fee

items.title: Confirm the speaker, subject, duration, introduction and content boundaries
items.detail: Agree the audience, tone, start time, speaking duration, questions, host introduction and any material or accessibility requirements.

items.label: Which entertainer, speaker or supplier is preferred, and who is the contact?
What will the external entertainment cost, including travel, equipment, accommodation or other expenses?
How will the external entertainer or speaker be paid?

options.label: Card or bank payment in advance

items.title: Book the external entertainer or speaker and record the complete agreement
items.detail: Confirm the date, performance and setup times, fee, deposit, cancellation terms, technical rider, insurance where relevant, contact details and what each party supplies.

items.title: Authorise the entertainment cost and arrange the agreed deposit or payment
items.detail: Give Accounts the supplier, agreed amount, due date, payment method and evidence needed for the event P&L and final reconciliation.

sections.title: Room, technical setup and event-day delivery

items.label: What performer or speaker space arrangements are required?
items.helpText: Record room choice, seating direction, top tables and table coverings in Clubhouse. Select only the performer, speaker or supplier-specific requirements here.

options.label: Supplier vehicle, loading or early access
No change from the standard room setup

items.label: What technical equipment or services are required?

options.label: Dedicated power, cables or safe cable routing

items.label: Who will be the entertainer or speaker's named club contact on the day?

items.title: Add the entertainment, introductions, breaks and finish time to the event running order
items.detail: Make the hand-offs between food service, announcements, entertainment and close-down explicit, and brief everyone affected.

items.title: Confirm performer access, performance position and technical setup with the Clubhouse team
items.detail: Translate the entertainment brief and supplier rider into a timed technical plan covering the stage or performance position, dance-floor clearance, power, cable safety, loading and access. Use the shared Clubhouse plan for room and seating layout.

staffBriefing.instruction: Prepare the agreed performer access, stage or speaker position and technical equipment before the entertainer or speaker arrives; follow the separate Clubhouse plan for seating and special tables.

items.title: Complete the soundcheck and technical test before guests need the room
items.detail: Test every microphone, playback source, presentation, light and connection with the person who will use it, and keep a workable fallback.

staffBriefing.instruction: Complete the soundcheck and test every required microphone, playback source, light and connection before guests need the room.

items.title: Receive the entertainer or speaker and manage the agreed event-day programme
items.detail: Confirm arrival, access, setup, hospitality, introductions, cues, payment hand-off where applicable and the agreed finish time.

staffBriefing.instruction: Receive the entertainer or speaker, show them the agreed facilities and manage the event-day running order.

modules.title: Clubhouse
modules.description: Room reservations, seating layouts, special tables, room dressing and audio-visual setup.

items.label: Which clubhouse rooms or areas need to be reserved or prepared?
items.helpText: Select every area that the Clubhouse team will need to make ready for the event.

items.label: Which other clubhouse room or area is required?
Will guests eat a served or pre-arranged meal while seated at tables?
items.helpText: This controls dining-specific tablecloth and seating-chart work. Record the physical seating direction separately below.

items.label: Does seating need to be laid out or rearranged specifically for the event?
How should the seating be arranged?

options.label: Rows facing the television or screens
Rows facing the rear of the room or top-table position

items.label: What additional seating or layout instructions should the Clubhouse team follow?
items.helpText: For example, record an unusual orientation, reserved spaces, mixed layouts or accessibility requirements.

items.label: Is a top or board table required?
items.helpText: This will normally be required for an AGM, member forum or another event where board members or speakers face the room.

items.label: How many seats are required at the top table?
Which covering, if any, is required for the top, board or prize table?
items.helpText: This records the table covering only. Prize and trophy display requirements remain in Presentation and prizes.

items.label: What table covering is required?

items.title: Agree and record the clubhouse room, seating and special-table plan
items.detail: Record the selected room or areas, seating direction, dining layout, top-table seat count, table coverings and any access requirements so that staff have one unambiguous setup plan.

items.title: Ensure dining tablecloths and table decorations are available
Prepare a seating chart and assign table numbers if necessary
Confirm the required top-table or presentation-table covering is available
items.detail: Locate and check the recorded club cloth, plain tablecloth or other covering in time for the room setup.

items.title: Prepare the selected clubhouse room, seating and special tables to the agreed layout
items.detail: Use the recorded room plan, including seating direction, dining tables, top-table seat count and selected coverings where required.

staffBriefing.instruction: Prepare the selected room or areas exactly as recorded, including the seating direction, dining layout, top table, seat count and table covering where required.

items.title: Complete the final room-layout and fire-exit safety check before guests arrive
items.detail: Walk every prepared area after setup and make sure all fire exits, escape routes, doorways and access aisles are completely clear. Move any chair, table, decoration, cable or equipment that creates an obstruction.

staffBriefing.instruction: After completing the room setup, walk every prepared area and confirm that all fire exits, escape routes, doorways and access aisles are completely clear.

items.title: Return the room, seating and special tables to the standard layout
items.detail: After the event, remove the temporary top table or special covering where used and return furniture in each prepared area to its normal position.

staffBriefing.instruction: Remove temporary seating, special tables and coverings, then return every prepared area to its normal layout.

items.label: Is there a specific theme that the room should be dressed for?

items.label: Do we need to coordinate the decorations with an external party, such as client-provided decorations or an external vendor?

items.title: Confirm theme and decoration requirements with the client or organiser

items.label: Are there any items that need to be ordered to complete the decorations?

items.title: Order supplies to dress the room
items.detail: Create as many individual tasks as are useful if several separate items must be ordered.

items.title: Set up decorations according to the agreed theme

staffBriefing.instruction: Dress the room using the agreed theme and decoration plan before guests arrive.

items.title: Update the staff briefing in relation to decorating the room

items.label: Do the decorations need to be removed after the event?

items.title: Remove decorations and return the room to its standard setup

staffBriefing.instruction: Remove the event decorations and return the room to its standard setup.

items.label: Will a specific channel, such as a sports event, need to be displayed on the screens?
items.helpText: This is about operational viewing during the event. Promotional use of the clubhouse screens is chosen in Communications.

items.title: Set up and display the specified channel during the event and record the channel in the plan

staffBriefing.instruction: Set the agreed television channel or stream on the specified display and confirm it is working before the event.

items.detail: Consider seasonal items, event type, guest preferences, budget and dietary restrictions.

items.label: How many food covers are required for the event?
items.helpText: Use the confirmed catering number rather than the broader attendance estimate, whether food is provided by the club or an external supplier.

items.label: What food and meal choices have been agreed for the event?
items.helpText: Record the wording the catering provider, bar and front-of-house teams need—for example each main choice, sides and desserts.

items.label: At what time should food service begin?
What dietary, allergen or alternative-meal requirements must the catering provider and service team know?
items.helpText: Record confirmed requirements or state that none are currently known; do not include unnecessary personal medical information, whether food is provided internally or externally.

items.title: Complete the kitchen and food-service setup for the agreed menu

staffBriefing.instruction: Complete food preparation and service setup for the recorded covers, menu choices, service time and dietary requirements.

items.title: Prepare and serve the agreed event menu

staffBriefing.instruction: Prepare and serve the agreed meal choices at the recorded service time, including the confirmed dietary alternatives.

items.label: Are printed menus required?

items.title: Create the printed menu design
Arrange for the menu to be printed

items.label: Will a separate digital menu be displayed inside the clubhouse during food service?
items.helpText: This is an operational food-service display, not the decision about promoting the event on the clubhouse screens.

items.title: Design the food-service digital menu and set it up on the agreed clubhouse display

staffBriefing.instruction: Display the agreed food-service menu on the selected clubhouse screen before ordering begins.

items.title: Include information about the menu in the staff briefing

items.label: When will orders be taken?
Where will orders be taken?

items.title: Set up an order collection method with the Pro Shop staff
items.detail: Ensure Pro Shop staff know the cut-off time for collecting orders, especially where the kitchen is working to a tight schedule.

staffBriefing.instruction: Collect meal orders using the agreed method and cut-off time, then pass them to the kitchen.

items.title: Arrange a system for transferring orders to the kitchen

staffBriefing.instruction: Receive and process orders from the Professional Shop using the agreed transfer method.

items.title: Set up an order collection method with the event organiser
items.detail: Agree whether individual meal choices need to be linked to named people or whether only the total quantity of each meal is required.

items.title: Set up an order collection method for the bar staff

staffBriefing.instruction: Collect meal orders at the bar using the agreed method and pass them to the kitchen.

items.label: Should vouchers be issued to be used in exchange for food or drink?

items.title: Design and print a sufficient number of food vouchers, including spares

items.label: Where will the vouchers be issued?
Will there be a charge for the meal?
items.helpText: This is the food charge within the voucher process. If food is included in a paid admission price, record that inclusion in Admission as well.

items.title: Distribute vouchers and advise guests regarding the payment method

staffBriefing.instruction: Distribute the food or drink vouchers at the agreed point and explain how guests should use them.

items.title: Collect all meal payments and provide them to the accounts team

staffBriefing.instruction: Collect the meal payments, complete the agreed cash or card handover and provide the totals to Accounts.

modules.title: Bookings, tickets and admission payments
modules.description: Decide whether attendees must book and/or pay, how places or tickets are made available, what people must do to register and how admission is managed.

items.label: Which arrangements apply to attending the event?
items.helpText: Select both options when attendees must reserve a place and also pay an entry charge. An advance ticket purchase counts as booking a place, even if no separate registration form is used.
items.example: A free AGM may require members to reserve a place; a party may require a paid named booking; a pay-on-the-door event may only require an entry charge.

options.label: Attendees must book, register, reserve or RSVP
Attendees will be charged for entry

items.label: Is entry free for certain attendee categories?
Which attendee categories have free entry?
items.helpText: Select every category that may attend without paying. Every category not selected here will need an agreed entry price.

items.title: Set the entry price for each attendee category that is not free
items.detail: Use the free-entry categories recorded above. Agree and record the price for every unticked category, including what each price includes, before the booking or ticket information is published.

reviewSummary.title: Free-entry categories and prices
reviewSummary.instruction: Review who has free entry, record the agreed price for every remaining category in the task notes, then confirm the prices.
reviewSummary.notesPlaceholder: For example: Members £8; visitors £12; children free

fields.label: Prices required for
fields.allSelectedText: None — all listed categories have free entry

items.label: What is the maximum number of places available?
items.helpText: Record the total event capacity across both free and paid attendees.

items.label: How will attendees access and complete the booking, registration or ticket process?
items.helpText: Choose every route people may use. Communications channels used to advertise the event are selected separately in Communications.

items.label: What must an attendee do to secure a place or buy entry?
items.helpText: Describe the steps, working link or contact, information to provide and payment point where applicable. The confirmation method is recorded separately below.
items.example: Complete the member booking form, pay online and retain the confirmation email; or telephone the office to be added to the free guest list.

items.label: When should advance booking, registration or ticket sales open?
When should advance booking, registration or ticket sales close?
How will attendees know their booking or advance purchase is confirmed, and what should they retain or show on arrival?
items.helpText: Record whether confirmation is a named guest-list entry, email, ticket, receipt, QR code or another proof of booking or purchase.

items.title: Approve the attendance process and event capacity
items.detail: Check that the attendee journey and total capacity are clear and workable. Where entry is charged, confirm the separate price-setting task is complete before prices or tickets are advertised.

items.title: Set up and test the agreed booking, registration or advance-ticket route
items.detail: Create the agreed booking or ticket record, apply capacity and opening or closing dates, test the complete attendee journey and give the working link or instructions to Communications.

sections.title: Booking and admission details for communications

items.label: What exact booking, registration or purchase information must be published?
items.helpText: Provide the approved public wording: the working link or contact, price where applicable, what is included, capacity or closing date and how confirmation works. The Communications module controls which channels publish it.

items.label: What cancellation or refund position should purchasers be told?

options.label: Full refund if the club cancels
Transfer to a new date or refund

items.title: Provide the approved attendance, booking and any price instructions for event communications
items.detail: Create one approved statement for the Communications Centre and attendee confirmations so every selected channel uses the same booking route, price where applicable and attendance conditions.

items.title: Agree and publish the ticket cancellation, transfer and refund terms
items.detail: Resolve the policy before taking money and make the purchaser-facing wording clear enough to use if the event changes.

sections.title: Payment and admission on the day

items.label: When can attendees pay the admission charge?

options.label: Charged to a member or customer account

items.label: Which payment methods will be accepted?
How will bookings or tickets be checked, and how will walk-ins or door sales be handled?
Is a cash float or secure cash handover required for door payments?

items.title: Prepare the admission desk, booking or ticket checks and any door-payment facilities
items.detail: Assign named people, provide the final attendee list, define how walk-ins and complimentary places are approved and, where needed, test the payment facilities before doors open.

staffBriefing.instruction: Set up the admission desk with the final guest list or ticket checks and any required payment facilities before doors open.

items.title: Prepare, record and securely hand over the admission cash float
items.detail: Record the opening float, who receives it, how cash is kept secure and who counts and returns it after admissions close.

staffBriefing.instruction: Record and securely hand over the admission float before doors open.

items.title: Reconcile admission payments, refunds and complimentary entries against attendance
items.detail: Record the final admission income in Event Finances, explain differences between payments and attendance, and provide cash, card and online totals to Accounts.

staffBriefing.instruction: Reconcile admission payments, refunds and complimentary entries against the final attendance.

modules.title: Communications
modules.description: Choose the channels for the event, create the corresponding Communications Centre work, and plan any final attendee information.

items.label: Who needs to hear about the event?
Does any planned member or attendee communication depend on material or a service that must be prepared first?
items.helpText: Choose Yes when the message needs to link to, include or ask members to use something that is not yet ready.
items.example: A questionnaire or feedback form, ticket, booking or RSVP service, information page, downloadable document, or a tested link and QR code.

dontKnowTask.title: Decide what must be ready before event communications are released
dontKnowTask.detail: Check the intended response or action with the organiser and Communications team, then replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: What needs to be ready before communications can be released?
items.helpText: Select the things the communication depends on, rather than the channels that will carry it. Ticket prices and payment decisions remain in Admission.

options.label: Ticket sales, payment page or purchase route
Information page, downloadable document or terms
QR-code destination, short link or trackable link
Reply mailbox, telephone contact or monitored response route

items.label: What exactly must be prepared, and who owns it?
items.helpText: Record the purpose, intended audience, owner and any approval or closing date that the person preparing it needs to know.
items.example: Create a question form for the member forum, agree who will review submissions and the closing date, then provide the approved link before the member email is sent.

items.title: Confirm every prerequisite is ready before member or attendee communications are released
items.detail: Coordinate with the operational owner of each selected form, booking route, page, document or service. Where booking, ticketing or attendee-feedback work already exists, verify that task rather than recreating it. Test the final link and QR destination, confirm approvals and data or privacy handling, and record the working URL or file in task notes before publishing.

items.label: Should the event be promoted on the clubhouse digital screens?

items.title: Prepare and schedule the clubhouse-screen campaign in the Communications Centre
items.detail: Create or approve the digital-screen artwork, choose its display dates and send it to the clubhouse screens.

items.label: Should members be emailed about the event?

items.title: Prepare, test and send the member email from the Communications Centre
items.detail: Generate or draft the email, review its event details and artwork, select the intended membership audience, send a test and then send the approved message.

items.label: Should the event be promoted on social media?

items.title: Prepare the social-media campaign and approved square artwork in the Communications Centre
items.detail: Use the approved campaign style and square artwork to prepare the social copy and agree when and where it will be published.

items.label: Should the event be published in the Member Diary?

items.title: Prepare and publish the Member Diary entry from the Communications Centre
items.detail: Generate or draft the member-facing diary entry, review the date, times, artwork and HTML content, and publish the approved entry.

items.label: Do attendees need final instructions before the event?
items.helpText: Choose Yes when attendees need practical information shortly before arrival, rather than another promotional message.
items.example: Arrival time, parking, dress code, what to bring, meal choices, payment on the night or where to report on arrival.

items.title: Send final attendee instructions covering timings, arrival, dress, payment and any event-specific information

modules.title: Staffing and responsibilities
modules.description: Make event-day ownership explicit so important jobs do not remain assumed or unassigned.

items.label: Who is responsible for coordinating staffing and any rota changes for this event?
items.helpText: This may be the event coordinator or the relevant department lead; it is separate from the person leading the event on the day.

items.label: Has the event-day lead been agreed?
items.helpText: The event-day lead must be one named person with clear authority to coordinate the event while it is taking place.
items.example: The person staff contact when a decision or response is needed during setup, the event or close-down.

items.label: Who is the event-day lead?
items.helpText: Choose the person who has accepted the role, not a department or shared responsibility.

items.title: Assign the event-day lead and make their authority and responsibilities clear
items.detail: Identify one person, confirm that they accept the role, then return to the Staffing questions and record their name as the event-day lead.

items.label: Are there specific arrival, setup, registration, service, presentation or close-down jobs that must be allocated?
items.helpText: This records what each person must do. The staffing and rota questions separately confirm who is attending and when.
items.example: Staff the registration desk, meet an entertainer, manage a presentation, clear decorations or hand over to the closing keyholder.

items.title: Create the event-day duty list and assign every named job to an individual
items.detail: List each practical duty, when and where it happens, who owns it and who they report to. This duty list complements the staff rota rather than replacing it.

items.label: Is a formal staff or volunteer briefing required?

items.title: Prepare and issue the final event briefing with timings, roles, contacts and contingency arrangements

items.label: Will additional staff or volunteers be needed beyond the normal rota?
items.helpText: Include extra people, longer shifts, earlier starts, later finishes or people temporarily covering a different role. Record detailed kitchen and bar demand in the Catering questions as well.

items.label: Which teams need additional or changed cover?
What additional or changed cover is expected, and during which times?
items.helpText: Record enough detail to cost the change and turn it into named shifts.
items.example: Two extra bar staff from 18:00–23:30 and two volunteers on arrivals from 18:30–19:30.

items.title: Agree, cost and authorise the additional staffing or volunteer cover
items.detail: Confirm the required headcount, roles, named people, shift times, breaks and handovers. Obtain approval for any additional hours or cost and record the estimate in Event Finances.

items.label: Have all affected staff rotas and volunteer schedules been updated and accepted for the event?
items.helpText: Answer Yes only when named people, start and finish times, breaks, handovers and any additional hours have been confirmed.
items.example: The normal rota may be used, but it still needs checking against the event timetable and duties.

items.title: Create or update the affected rotas and confirm that every shift has been accepted
items.detail: Cover the event from first setup through final handover or lock-up, including start and finish times, breaks, service peaks and named responsibility for each shift. Then return to Staffing and mark the rota answer Yes.

items.label: Does the confirmed cover run from first access and setup through final handover or lock-up?
items.helpText: Check service peaks, breaks, shift handovers and close-down rather than only the advertised event start and finish times.

items.title: Resolve the remaining gaps in setup, service, break, handover or close-down cover
items.detail: Compare the confirmed rotas with the complete event timetable, assign the uncovered periods and then return to Staffing to confirm that whole-event cover is in place.

items.label: Has fallback and escalation cover been agreed if a key person is absent or delayed?
items.helpText: Consider the event lead, opening and closing keyholders, cash handlers, first aider and any role that cannot safely be left uncovered.

items.title: Agree replacement and escalation cover for critical staffing roles
items.detail: Identify which roles cannot be left uncovered, nominate replacements or escalation contacts and make sure the event lead and affected teams know the arrangement.

items.label: What opening and early-access arrangement applies to this event?
items.helpText: Consider staff setup, supplier deliveries and entertainer access before the club would normally be open.

items.label: Who will open the building and provide the early access?
items.helpText: Choose an authorised person who has accepted responsibility for access and security.

items.title: Arrange authorised early-opening and access cover
items.detail: Confirm the required access time, nominate an authorised keyholder and then return to Staffing to record the confirmed person.

items.title: Open the clubhouse and provide the agreed early access
items.detail: Assign this duty to the person recorded as the opening keyholder. Open only the required areas, manage access and hand over to the normal duty team when they arrive.

staffBriefing.instruction: Open the agreed clubhouse areas at the recorded time, manage early access and hand over securely to the normal duty team.

items.label: What final closing and lock-up arrangement applies to this event?
items.helpText: The answer must cover the period after guests leave while cash, equipment, cleaning or room close-down is still taking place.

options.label: The event keyholder will complete final lock-up
The event team will hand over to the later duty closer
Closing and lock-up still need arranging

items.label: Who has final responsibility for closing and locking up?
items.helpText: Choose the authorised person who will remain until the event team has finished or accepted the formal handover.

items.title: Arrange a named authorised closer and lock-up handover
items.detail: Confirm who remains responsible after guests leave, how long close-down will take and who holds the keys or alarm authority. Then return to Staffing and record the arrangement and named person.

items.title: Remain through close-down and complete the final clubhouse lock-up
items.detail: Assign this duty to the person recorded as the closing keyholder. Confirm guests and staff have left, complete the agreed security checks, set the alarm where applicable and secure the building.

staffBriefing.instruction: Remain until event close-down is complete, complete the agreed security checks, set the alarm where applicable and lock the clubhouse.

items.title: Complete the closing handover to the named duty closer
items.detail: Tell the named closer what remains occupied or outstanding, transfer any keys, cash or incident information securely and obtain their acceptance of final lock-up responsibility.

staffBriefing.instruction: Complete a clear handover to the named duty closer, including occupied areas, outstanding work, keys, cash and any incident information.

modules.title: Safety and contingency
modules.description: Event-specific safety, safeguarding, first-aid and fallback planning.

items.label: Does the event introduce risks that require a specific risk assessment or control plan?

items.title: Complete the event risk assessment and record any required controls

items.label: Will children or junior members take part in the event?

items.title: Confirm the safeguarding arrangements, supervision and responsible contacts for juniors

items.label: Could weather materially affect the event or require a fallback plan?

items.title: Agree the weather contingency, cancellation decision process and communication route

modules.title: Close-down and follow-up
modules.description: Return the club to normal, settle outstanding items and capture lessons for next time.

items.label: Does anything already identified in this event plan, or anything else, need to be reset, removed, returned or cleared after the event?
items.helpText: Review the arrangements already identified elsewhere in the plan. Answer Yes if any of them must be reversed or if any additional close-down work is needed.

planningContext.title: Relevant setup and end-of-event arrangements already recorded
planningContext.description: This is assembled automatically from the answers elsewhere in this event plan.
planningContext.emptyText: No temporary setup or end-of-event arrangement has been identified from the current answers yet.
planningContext.falseAnswerWarning: Earlier answers indicate that temporary arrangements exist. Before keeping No, confirm that they may remain in place or are already covered by routine departmental closing duties.
planningContext.footerText: Use this as the starting point for close-down. Existing specialist tasks remain in place and should be coordinated rather than duplicated.

fields.label: Dining setup
fields.trueText: Seated dining and dining tables are planned

fields.label: Seating
fields.trueText: Event-specific seating will be laid out or rearranged

fields.label: Top or board table
fields.trueText: A top or board table will be set up

fields.label: Prize display
fields.trueText: A prize or trophy table will be set up

fields.label: Room dressing
fields.trueText: The room will be dressed or decorated for the event

fields.label: Decoration removal
fields.trueText: Decorations are already marked for removal
fields.falseText: The current plan says decorations do not need removing

fields.label: Arrival signage
fields.trueText: Arrival or registration signage will be positioned

fields.label: Clubhouse screens
fields.trueText: A specific channel or stream will be set up

fields.label: Food supplier
fields.trueText: An external food supplier will require a load-out or handover

fields.label: Food service
fields.trueText: Food preparation and service areas will have been used

fields.label: Vouchers
fields.trueText: Food or drink vouchers will be issued

fields.label: Cash handover
fields.trueText: An admission cash float will require reconciliation and handover

items.label: Which areas, arrangements or materials need to be cleared, reset, returned or handed over?
items.helpText: Select everything the close-down lead must coordinate, including work already represented by a specialist departmental task.

options.label: Dining, top or prize tables and coverings
Decorations, temporary signs or printed material
Course signage, markers, temporary features, lighting or equipment
Screens, PA, microphones, cables or other technical equipment
Kitchen, bar, food-service areas, supplier equipment or waste
Admission desk, cash, lists or registration material
External supplier or performer load-out and collection

items.label: What should the close-down team do with the selected items or areas?
items.helpText: Record the required end state, storage location, collection or handover so that completion is unambiguous.
items.example: Return chairs to the standard layout, put the club cloth back in the office and leave the hired PA ready for collection by 09:00.

items.label: Is any additional clear-up or recovery work needed beyond reversing the arrangements identified above?
items.helpText: Consider cleaning, rubbish, recycling, lost property, supplier collection, damaged equipment and anything that routine closing duties will not cover.

items.label: What additional clear-up or recovery work is required?
Who will coordinate and sign off the close-down on the day?
items.helpText: Choose the named person who will check the selected actions, coordinate departmental handovers and report anything still outstanding.

items.title: Complete and sign off the agreed event close-down
items.detail: Coordinate the selected actions and existing departmental tasks, confirm required handovers and collections, and record anything that could not be returned to its agreed end state.

reviewSummary.title: Agreed close-down plan
reviewSummary.instruction: The named close-down lead coordinates the specialist teams and signs this off only when the selected actions and handovers are complete.

fields.label: Scope
fields.emptyText: Select what must be cleared, reset, returned or handed over

fields.label: Required end state
fields.emptyText: Record what the close-down team must do

fields.label: Additional clear-up needed
fields.emptyText: Confirm whether anything else is required

fields.label: Close-down lead
fields.emptyText: Choose the person responsible on the day

staffBriefing.instruction: Follow the agreed close-down scope and end-state instructions, complete each departmental handover and report anything outstanding to the named close-down lead.

items.label: Will anonymous attendee feedback be collected for this event?
items.helpText: The retrospective can create a reusable public link and QR code without asking attendees for names or contact details.

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether anonymous attendee feedback will be collected for this event
dontKnowTask.detail: Confirm the intended audience and how the link or QR code could be distributed, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.title: Agree the attendee feedback questions and prepare the event feedback link and QR code
items.detail: Open the event retrospective to create the anonymous form and check its closing date before it is shared.

items.title: Share the attendee feedback form and display its QR code where guests can use it
items.detail: Use the public link in follow-up communications, on event material or via a future membership or ticketing integration.

items.title: Review anonymous attendee feedback and approve the learning to carry into the next event
items.detail: Turn useful evidence into concise organiser-approved notes and map each one to the relevant planner section, question or task.

items.title: Complete the post-event retrospective and record financial and operational lessons
items.detail: Record what went well, what did not go well and what should improve next time. Include the event's financial result and any operational learning that should be carried into a future event.

advisoryRules.title: Players may return after catering closes
advisoryRules.message: Based on the tee sheet and expected round duration, competitors are expected to return until approximately {expectedLatestGolfFinish}. Normal catering closes at {cateringClosingTime}. Are you sure catering hours should not be extended?

advisoryRules.title: Food may be required before catering opens
advisoryRules.message: The event indicates food may be needed from {requiredCateringStart}, while normal catering opens at {cateringOpeningTime}. Are you sure catering hours should not be extended?

advisoryRules.title: Shotgun finish creates a concentrated clubhouse peak
advisoryRules.message: This event uses a shotgun start, so most players are expected back in the clubhouse at around {expectedLatestGolfFinish}. That creates a concentrated demand peak rather than a normal staggered return. Are you sure no additional catering or bar cover is needed?

fields.label: What can we improve for next time?
Should we run this event again?
